For new procurement, the cost of LPTs could range from roughly $15,0006 to $21,0007 per MVA8 (USITC 2024a), depending on unit rating, voltage class, country of origin, transportation needs and customization requirements. For a 100-MVA unit, this corresponds to approximately $1.5–$2.1 million per unit. In some cases, particularly for highly customized units with complex logistics, costs can reach as high as $40/kW , translating to about $4 million for a 100-MVA unit. A 2020 industry survey by the ac U.S. Department of Commerce found that GOES and CTC, two major components, each contribute about 25% of the total production cost of an LPT (Bureau of Industry and Security 2021). Logistics and transportation can account for approximately 3% to 20% (U.S. Department of Energy 2024) of the total cost of an LPT, depending on factors such as distance, routing, and escort requirements for oversized loads. Remote hydropower project facilities such as the ones in hilly terrains or rural parts of the country often face the highest logistical premiums due to limited rail access and complex road networks. Oversized transformer shipments typically require route surveys, permits, and, in some cases, infrastructure modifications, all of which add substantially to the final installed cost. For imported units, maritime shipping rates, port handling fees, and inland transportation can collectively add hundreds of thousands of dollars, particularly during periods of global supply chain disruption. Labor cost differentials by region also contribute to price variation. Assembly and installation labor rates in the Northeast and on the West Coast are typically 15% to 25% higher than in other parts of country, driven by prevailing wage rates and cost of living.
